intelligence.human_view: Two words — over and around — are the whole difference between a board that glows beautifully and a board with a wash poured across its face. The machine heard "around" when he said "over" and nearly removed the good glow while keeping the bad one. That is the failure inside the failure: not just a wrong glow, but a wrong hearing. His correction is the lesson — when he corrects the wording, the wording IS the correction. Repeat his word back, with the direction, before acting on it: over means over the top, around means around the outside, through means through the board, behind means behind the circle. Get the preposition right and the design follows; get it wrong and the round removes the beautiful thing and keeps the ugly one.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a glowing ring around a present — pretty, right? Now imagine someone pours glowing paint all over the top of the present so you can't see it anymore. The ring around is beautiful. The paint over the top ruins it. Shawn wants the ring around, not the paint over. And the shiny globe stays right where it is.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the purple light around the box is lovely — it makes the box glow like a jewel. But the light poured over the top of the board covers it up, like a blanket over something beautiful. Keep the light around it, keep the shine through it, keep the globe — just take the blanket off the top. Around, not over. Behind, not on top.
intelligence.naya_view: THE PURPLE GLOW OVER THE BOARD GOES. THE PURPLE GLOW AROUND THE BOX IS GREAT. THE SHINE THROUGH THE BOARD IS GREAT. GLOW LIVES UNDERNEATH, AROUND, BEHIND — NEVER OVER THE TOP.
